answer.rationale: Rollback is excluded by compliance since the security patch must stay. Regional failover risks write-path consistency during a settlement peak and memory_b2's precedent was about latency recovery during a general degradation, not heavy-write settlement traffic, so its applicability here is uncertain—worth checking the archived record before ruling it out entirely. Circuit breaking risks dropping customer writes, conflicting directly with the stated objective. Read-replica routing doesn't address write-path latency at all. Adding capacity (memory_b3) directly matches the failure mode—headroom provisioning absorbed a prior write/query surge without customer impact—and doesn't touch the protected release or risk write loss. I want to verify b3's original context (was it read or write path, and how fast did headroom take effect?) and b2's original context (did failover preserve in-flight writes or only recover latency) before committing, since sustained availability without losing writes is the binding constraint and archived specifics matter more than the consolidated summary.
